feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital communications CV with clear positioning, credible scope, and relevant public-sector leadership experience. It reads professionally and shows progression well, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear executive profile: the headline and summary quickly establish a strong niche in digital platforms, governance, analytics, and communications leadership.  
- Credible impact signals: examples like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and building an in-house studio add scale and substance.  
- Solid career progression: multiple promotions at NACo demonstrate trust, growth, and increasing responsibility.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition and tighten structure: “digital strategy/operations/governance/platforms” appears often across summary, competencies, skills, and roles. Consolidate overlapping sections, especially Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results. Include measurable improvements in traffic, engagement, efficiency, adoption, or cost savings where possible.  
- Fix writing/style inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” should lose the comma; “Ranked among the top public universities...” is weak/irrelevant filler; punctuation and formatting vary across bullets/sections. No major misspellings found, but style is inconsistent (e.g., “AI-enabled” vs. broader phrasing, bold-heavy footer, mixed section density).
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning and clear seniority, but the intro is slightly generic and repeats several themes already covered in the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web, analytics, and editorial systems for high-volume public-sector organizations. Leads digital governance, content operations, multimedia production, and AI-enabled user experiences that improve how complex, mission-driven institutions publish, measure, and scale communications.”
- Add one concrete proof point if space allows, such as “10,000+ page website,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with a more active, outcome-oriented verb like “modernizing,” “scaling,” or “leading.”
- Keep tense/style parallel: “web modernization, analytics, editorial systems, multimedia, and AI-enabled experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects.
- “Governance models and content operations” closely repeats the subtitle and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this section overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and making the categories more distinctive will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use sharper, parallel phrasing: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership
- Clarify technical/strategic blend: AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Consider replacing “content experiences” with “content discovery” or “user experiences” for clearer meaning.
- Keep style consistent by avoiding “&” if other sections primarily use “and.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This block substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; consider making it either more strategic/high-level or more capability-based, not both.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with multiple NACo roles and may be redundant unless tailored to target roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with work-experience bullets. Tightening phrasing and foregrounding outcomes, platforms, or scope will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, compact phrasing: “Built/Developed/Launched…” and keep each item to one crisp line.
- Add one concrete differentiator per project where possible: platform, audience, scale, or business purpose.
- Standardize style: use “AI-enabled,” “Drupal 10,” and spell out “10 x 20-foot” consistently.
- Consider this tighter version:  
  **AI Hybrid Search** Built an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat to improve policy-content discovery.  
  **We Are Counties Microsite** Developed a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources, and a modular architecture for future expansion.  
  **Organization Anniversary Campaign** Created a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10 x 20-foot interactive conference display integrated with the main site.  
  **Advocacy Video Series** Produced an ongoing advocacy video series spanning editorial planning, production, and distribution across web, email, and social.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search and Advocacy Video Series closely repeat achievements already covered in recent roles.
- “Built/Developed” campaign and microsite language overlaps with the current freelance entry; keep footer more selective or more outcome-focused.

items.content:
### Recent Projects

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and NACo entries. Tighten it around 3–4 highest-impact contributions and add outcomes or scale wherever possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client type: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcomes: “Built cross-team workflows, analytics, and governance systems that improved coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Combine Drupal/CMS bullets: “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits; also handled front-end implementation and production troubleshooting.”
- Make the AI/search work the capstone: “Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content modeling, and user-facing discovery experience.” Add metrics if available: users, pages, time saved, launches, adoption.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats prior NACo roles and the summary; keep only if tied to a distinct result.
- Footer project examples already cover microsites and AI search, so avoid repeating the same detail here verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles. Lead with the biggest enterprise wins: web modernization, analytics infrastructure, and operational governance.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing: quantify newsletter list size, social growth/engagement, studio output, cost savings, reporting speed, or governance efficiency.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce platform lists: “Built an enterprise analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, BI dashboards, and BigQuery to improve reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this at a more strategic/enterprise level.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with older multimedia bullets unless framed as first-time organizational capability at director level.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry is too close to the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Emphasize executional leadership and channel growth here, not broader governance/operations language already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter scope: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, supporting advocacy messaging and cross-team editorial execution.”
- Combine newsletter impact into one sharper bullet: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet to show ownership and channel-building: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing with clearer operational outcomes: “Coordinated editorial calendars across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving publishing consistency and campaign alignment.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Improved digital publishing workflows” overlaps with the Director role’s governance/publishing standards bullet.
- “Expanded weekly video updates” is similar to the 2015–2018 role; keep focus here on scaling/regularizing the series.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent experience. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and aligned to the most senior/recent strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, senior-level language tied to current positioning:  
  **• Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations**  
  **• Editorial governance and content operations**  
  **• Cross-channel communications leadership**  
  **• Audience-centered messaging and campaign planning**
- Cut “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” if you want to avoid sounding repetitive with other sections; fold that context into the first bullet instead.
- Keep to 4 bullets max; this section should scan fast and complement, not restate, the summary.
- If space allows, use “content operations” instead of “content planning” to better reflect leadership scope shown in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also repeats Core Competencies; consider differentiating with “cross-channel operations” or “campaign planning.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills block, make it more strategic, grouped, and tied to the candidate’s recent Drupal/CMS modernization and AI-search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint & Power Pages” → “Enterprise CMS platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages”
- Prioritize recent/high-value strengths first: “CMS modernization • Drupal development • API integrations • Workflow automation • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Tighten coding line: replace “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” with “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery)”
- Suggested rewrite: “- Enterprise CMS platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages - CMS modernization & front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) - API integrations, workflow automation & Airtable systems - AI-enabled search experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats many exact tools already listed in “Technical + IT”; keep this section higher-level, not exhaustive.
- “CMS modernization” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies, so avoid repeating identical phrasing elsewhere.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. This topline item should emphasize strategic application and decision-making impact, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis, and dashboarding across GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, and Microsoft Clarity.”
- Put the highest-value, recent strengths first: KPI design, executive/leadership reporting, analytics infrastructure, then tools.
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Executive dashboards” for sharper phrasing.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier: “for enterprise web performance and content decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills strategic and leave full tool inventory to Technical + IT.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader analytics language; combine as “SEO and digital performance analysis.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies (“multimedia production and livestream operations”) and Technical + IT (“Multimedia & Creative Tools”). Make this item more outcome-oriented and scoped to leadership-level delivery rather than listing basic capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward operational ownership and higher-value strengths: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio and PTZ camera operations • Virtual event production workflows”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to better match the NACo studio build and seniority.
- Change “Livestreaming” to “Livestream and hybrid event delivery” for stronger phrasing and clearer event context.
- Consider adding one differentiator if accurate: “Run-of-show planning” or “Multi-camera production” instead of generic “Studio operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies.
- Tool-specific detail is already covered in Technical + IT, so avoid listing software/hardware here unless it’s a true differentiator.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Use it to signal depth and recency—especially Drupal—rather than listing tools already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show proficiency level and emphasis: **Drupal (enterprise modernization, microsites, structured content) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, group by strength: **Primary: Drupal | Working knowledge: WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Consider replacing **GitHub Pages** with a more relevant platform only if used materially in recent roles; otherwise it can read lightweight beside enterprise CMS work.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; if “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, don’t repeat that phrase here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Topline Skills” entry listing the same platforms; differentiate by adding proficiency/context or remove one version.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent experience, so avoid overloading multiple sections with the same bare keyword list.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, and automation work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Rewrite as: **HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; they add little value and date the section.
- If accurate, consider adding one higher-signal qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. **front-end CMS implementation**, **tag deployment**, or **light serverless scripting**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; keep one version shorter or make this one more implementation-specific.
- “Workflow automation” is already covered elsewhere, so avoid adding broad automation language here unless tied to GitHub Actions or Cloudflare Workers.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize systems you actually used to build/coordinate workflows, not general collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Project Systems**
- Reorder by relevance/strength: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana**
- Move general collaboration tools out unless central to workflow design: **Slack • Teams**
- Cut lower-value/redundant tools or group them: **Basecamp • Trello** → include only if recently used or materially important

Possible rewrite:
**Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack/Teams workflow coordination**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack and Teams function more as collaboration tools than technical workflow systems, so they may fit better in a lighter “Collaboration Tools” line or be removed.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement capability. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and platform-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform naming for readability and consistency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add functional scope instead of more tools: **campaign automation, newsletter operations, segmentation, member communications**
- Optional stronger version: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp | Email automation, newsletter publishing, audience segmentation**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating newsletter scale or “tens of thousands” here; that impact is already covered in Work Experience.
- Don’t add broad “multi-channel communications” language here; it duplicates Core Competencies and recent role bullets.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is currently just a keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In Technical + IT, it should read as a tighter tools/category line, with less generic wording and clearer specialization.

Suggested edit
- Replace broad terms with more technical/credible phrasing: “SEO” → “SEO analysis,” “Dashboarding” → “Reporting dashboards” or remove if redundant.
- Group by function for readability: “GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • A/B testing • SEO analysis”
- Consider dropping the weakest/generic item (“Dashboarding”) since Looker Studio and Power BI already imply it.
- If accurate, strengthen with implementation-oriented terms: “GA4 implementation,” “tagging/measurement,” or “conversion analysis” instead of generic optimization language.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This is nearly duplicated by “Topline Skills – Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Keep one more strategic and this one purely tool-based.
- “A/B testing” and “SEO” are useful, but if not evidenced elsewhere in recent roles, they may feel less credible than the analytics stack.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational: emphasize team-building, early platform/content ownership, and any concrete scale or output.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Add measurable scope where possible: website refresh size/traffic, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, channels supported, or team size mentored.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic terms like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows”; replace with outcomes such as improved publishing speed, consistency, or production capacity.
- Example: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations. Contributed to a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; if kept here, frame this as launching or piloting the format.
- Avoid repeating governance/workflow language already used more strongly in later NACo entries.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize innovation/program support and the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator.

Suggested edit
- Recast to foreground scope and ownership: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast launch the impact statement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Trim vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a more specific support verb such as “produced” or “developed” only if accurate.
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or types of projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” is redundant with later roles focused on video/multimedia production.
- Avoid overstating digital leadership here; later NACo roles already show progression into broader digital ownership.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
